chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Four categories of people upon whom the complete prayer is obligatory, whether they are in travel or in residence: the hirer (of animals), the worker (of it), the shepherd, and the mailman, because it is their occupation.'

key_terms.التَّمَامُ: Complete prayer (performing all four rak'ahs without shortening)
key_terms.الْمُكَارِي: The hirer (one who hires animals for transport)

ai.seo_question: Who is obligated to perform complete prayer during travel according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the juristic principle that the nature of one's occupation can supersede the standard rules of travel, specifically exempting the sailor, hirer, shepherd, and estate worker from shortening their prayers (Qasr) because their work constitutes a state of continuous travel. In Shia fiqh, this ruling underscores the flexibility of Islamic law, recognizing that for these professionals, the 'travel' condition is inherent to their livelihood rather than a temporary state, thus requiring the full four-rak'ah prayer as if they were in residence.
